lines.trans: You heard from Tae-ho that I asked you to help me out with the special concert, right?
I have not heard a thing about it?
I am putting on the Family Month special concert this time!
All sorts of high-ranking figures and even our station president are attending as honored guests!
My heart is fluttering with excitement, Ye-jin!
Hey, why on earth would I get dragged into that?
We need a producer to direct the stage!
What are you talking about—you are supposed to direct that yourself!
Then who is going to escort all those countless VIP guests?
Oh, good for you—so which performers are going up on stage?

examples.trans: Listen well.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: common in TV/radio programming and magazines

examples.trans: There is a special broadcast tonight.
I watched the Lunar New Year special program.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 태호 형한테 얘기 들었지, 나 특집 쇼 하는 거 좀 도와달라고?
examples.trans: You heard from Tae-ho that I asked you to help me out with the special concert, right?
Here the word for 'show' is key.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

examples.trans: I want to who will help right now.
How about trying to who will help together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Used before time nouns like 이번 주 (this week)

examples.trans: There is a meeting this Friday.
I will definitely succeed this time.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 나 이번에 가정의 달 특집 쇼 하잖아!
examples.trans: I am putting on the Family Month special concert this time!
Here the word for 'of the family' is key.
I am busy this month.

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: My heart is fluttering with excitement, Ye-jin!
This expression comes from 'am fluttering with excitement'.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Points to a place near the listener, and in casual or brisk speech is used to call out to someone whose name you do not know. RR: geogi.

examples.trans: Hey, you there, just a moment!
How is the atmosphere there?

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 야, 근데 거기 내가 왜 끼냐고?
examples.trans: Hey, why on earth would I get dragged into that?
This expression comes from 'get roped in?'.

meanings.note: physical performance stage
a musical or show performance on stage

examples.trans: We have lots of stages that day.
Today's stage performance was really great.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: We need a producer to direct the stage!
This expression comes from 'to direct'.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: in expressions like 뭔 소리야? ('what are you talking about?')
audible sound made by people or things

examples.trans: Suddenly a strange sound was heard.

examples.text: 말도 안 되는 소리 하지 마.
examples.trans: Don't talk nonsense.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Used to emphasize an adjective or verb.
